overview.intro:
Chapter 87 covers road vehicles and their parts: tractors (8701), buses (8702), cars and SUVs (8703), trucks (8704), special-purpose vehicles (8705), chassis, bodies and parts (8706–8708), works trucks (8709), tanks (8710), motorcycles and e-bikes (8711), bicycles (8712), wheelchairs (8713), cycle parts (8714), strollers (8715) and trailers (8716). Base rates are low (cars 2.5%, most parts 2.5%) except for trucks of 8704, which pay **25%**.

What decides the cost is **Section 232**. Since April 3, 2025 **cars, SUVs, minivans and light trucks** pay **+25%** (9903.94.01), and since May 3, 2025 **auto parts** pay **+25%** (9903.94.05). Trade deals cap both at **15% in total** for Japan, the EU and South Korea (Taiwan for parts), and the UK pays **10%** on 100,000 cars a year. USMCA-qualifying cars from Canada and Mexico pay 25% only on their non-U.S. content, and USMCA-qualifying parts pay nothing. Since November 1, 2025 **medium- and heavy-duty trucks**, road tractors and their parts pay **+25%** (9903.74.01, 9903.74.08) and **buses +10%**. Trailers, farm tractors and some parts pay the Section 232 **metals** duty instead (25%, or 15% total for farm equipment). These Section 232 goods do not pay the 2026 Section 301 duties.

China pays more: **127.5%** on electric cars (100% Section 301 + 25%), **52.5%** on gasoline cars and car parts. **71 lines are outside Section 232**: motorcycles, bicycles, wheelchairs, strollers, cycle parts and tanks, which pay the 2026 Section 301 duties (10% or 12.5%) for most countries. Canada pays an extra **50%** (Section 338) on golf carts, snow vehicles and off-road vehicles, and its motorcycles over 800 cc are **banned** since September 29, 2026. Antidumping and countervailing duties on golf carts, chassis, brake drums, steel wheels and van trailers are not part of this table.

productGroups.label: Tractors (farm, road, crawler)
productGroups.blurb: Farm tractors, road tractors for semi-trailers, crawler and single-axle tractors: 38 lines, Free or 4%. Road tractors pay the 25% truck tariff; farm tractors pay 15% total and other tractors 25% under the Section 232 metals equipment rules.

productGroups.label: Buses (10 or more persons)
productGroups.blurb: Buses and vans for 10 or more people: 10 lines at 2%. All pay +10% under Section 232 (9903.74.02) from November 1, 2025, with or without USMCA.

productGroups.label: Cars, SUVs, golf carts & ATVs
productGroups.blurb: Passenger cars, SUVs, minivans, electric and hybrid cars, plus snowmobiles, golf carts and ATVs: 73 lines at 2.5%. Cars pay +25% (Japan, EU, Korea 15% total; UK 10% in quota); Chinese EVs 127.5%.

productGroups.label: Trucks & pickups
productGroups.blurb: Pickups, vans, dump trucks and heavy trucks: 38 lines, mostly 25% (the "chicken tax" rate) plus 25% under Section 232: 50% for most countries; Japan, EU and Korea light trucks stay at 25%.

productGroups.label: Special-purpose vehicles (cranes, fire trucks)
productGroups.blurb: Mobile cranes, drilling derricks, fire trucks, concrete mixers and other special-purpose trucks: 8 lines, all Free. Some pay the 25% truck tariff, cranes and derricks the 25% metals equipment rate.

productGroups.label: Chassis with engines
productGroups.blurb: Chassis fitted with engines: 9 lines, Free to 4%. Car chassis pay the 25% auto parts duty, truck chassis the 25% truck tariff.

productGroups.label: Bodies & cabs
productGroups.blurb: Bodies and cabs: 9 lines, Free to 4%. Auto parts duty (25%) for car bodies, truck parts duty (25%) for truck cabs.

productGroups.label: Auto parts & accessories
productGroups.blurb: Bumpers, body parts, brakes, gearboxes, axles, wheels, suspension, radiators, steering and airbags: 121 lines, mostly 2.5%. Car parts pay 25% (Japan, EU, Korea, Taiwan 15%; UK 10%; USMCA parts Free); truck parts 25%.

productGroups.label: Works trucks (forklift-type, airport)
productGroups.blurb: Self-propelled works trucks (factory, warehouse, airport) and parts: 7 lines, all Free. Some pay the 25% truck tariff.

productGroups.label: Tanks & armored vehicles
productGroups.blurb: Tanks and other armored fighting vehicles: 3 lines, all Free. No Section 232 duty.

productGroups.label: Motorcycles, mopeds & e-bikes
productGroups.blurb: Motorcycles, mopeds, scooters and e-bikes: 15 lines, Free or 2.4%. Outside Section 232; the 2026 Section 301 duties apply. Canadian motorcycles over 800 cc are banned from import since September 29, 2026.

productGroups.label: Bicycles
productGroups.blurb: Bicycles: 8 lines, 3.7% to 11%. Outside Section 232; 2026 Section 301 duties apply; Chinese bicycles also pay 25% (List 3).

productGroups.label: Wheelchairs
productGroups.blurb: Wheelchairs, manual and powered: 3 lines, all Free. Outside Section 232.

productGroups.label: Motorcycle, bicycle & wheelchair parts
productGroups.blurb: Parts of motorcycles, bicycles and wheelchairs (frames, wheels, brakes, saddles, derailleurs): 31 lines, Free to 10%. Outside Section 232.

productGroups.label: Baby strollers & parts
productGroups.blurb: Baby carriages, strollers and parts: 2 lines at 4.4%. Outside Section 232; Chinese strollers pay only the 2026 Section 301 duty (12.5%).

productGroups.label: Trailers, semi-trailers & parts
productGroups.blurb: Semi-trailers, van and tank trailers, utility and boat trailers, wagons and trailer parts: 27 lines, Free to 5.7%. Most pay the Section 232 metals duty (25%); some parts the auto parts duty.

workedExamples.title: A $40,000 car from Japan
workedExamples.body: Japanese cars pay **15% in total** (9903.94.41) in place of the 2.5% base rate and the 25% Section 232 duty, under the U.S.–Japan agreement from September 16, 2025: **$6,000**. The same car from Taiwan, India or Thailand pays 2.5% + 25% = 27.5% ($11,000). The 2026 Section 301 duty does not apply to Section 232 vehicles.

workedExamples.title: A car built in Mexico, USMCA-qualifying
workedExamples.body: USMCA removes the 2.5% base rate, and Section 232 charges **25% only on the non-U.S. content** (9903.94.03) once Commerce has approved the U.S.-content value; the U.S. content enters at 0% (9903.94.02). Without an approval the duty is 25% of the full value. A non-qualifying Mexican car pays 27.5%.

workedExamples.title: A Chinese electric car
workedExamples.body: 2.5% base rate + **100%** Section 301 (U.S. note 31, 9903.91.03, since September 27, 2024) + **25%** Section 232 (9903.94.01) = **127.5%**. A Chinese gasoline car pays 2.5% + 25% (List 1) + 25% = 52.5%.

workedExamples.title: A pickup truck from Thailand or Japan
workedExamples.body: Light trucks carry a **25%** base rate, and Section 232 adds **25%**: **50%** from Thailand, the UK or most other countries. For Japan, the EU and Korea the deal caps the total at 15%, but because the base rate is already 25% no Section 232 duty is added: **25%**.

workedExamples.title: Gearbox parts from Germany, Japan or Mexico
workedExamples.body: As a car part: **15%** in total from Germany (EU, 9903.94.53) or Japan (9903.94.43); **Free** from Mexico or Canada with USMCA (9903.94.06); **27.5%** from India or Thailand; **52.5%** from China (25% Section 232 + 25% List 3). As a part for a heavy truck: 2.5% + 25% (9903.74.08), USMCA parts Free.

workedExamples.title: A heavy truck from Germany or Mexico
workedExamples.body: Trucks over 20 t G.V.W. pay the **25%** base rate plus **25%** Section 232 (9903.74.01) from November 1, 2025: **50%**. A USMCA-qualifying truck from Mexico or Canada pays 25% on its non-U.S. content only (9903.74.03) and no base rate. From China: 75%.

workedExamples.title: A road bicycle from Taiwan or China
workedExamples.body: Bicycles are outside Section 232. From Taiwan the 2026 Section 301 rate is **10% in place of** the 5.5% base rate (9903.05.76): **10%**. From China: 5.5% + 25% (List 3) + 12.5% (9903.05.31) = **43%**.

tariffUpdates.intro:
This page compares two editions of the tariff schedule, the **2025 Basic Edition** (in force January 1, 2025) and the current **2026 Revision 21** (in force October 9, 2026), and lists every extra duty that reaches Chapter 87 today. Base rates did not change: 396 of 402 lines are the same, and six statistical lines were added by splitting existing ones at the same rate.

The extra duties changed completely. In January 2025 a car paid its 2.5% base rate (China: +25% or +100% for EVs). Proclamation 10908 added **25% on cars and light trucks from April 3, 2025** and on **auto parts from May 3, 2025**, with USMCA parts exempt and USMCA vehicles charged only on non-U.S. content. Deals then capped the total at **15%** for the EU (August 1, 2025), Japan (September 16, 2025), Korea (November 1, 2025) and Taiwan's parts (May 1, 2026), and set **10%** for UK cars within a quota. Proclamation 10984 added **25% on medium- and heavy-duty trucks and parts and 10% on buses from November 1, 2025**. The IEEPA duties ended on **February 24, 2026**; the 2026 Section 301 duties skip Section 232 vehicles and parts. In 2026 Canada's Section 338 duty and an import ban reached golf carts, off-road vehicles and large motorcycles.

Antidumping and countervailing duty orders on golf carts, chassis, brake drums and steel wheels, and new investigations on van trailers, are listed below for reference and **not included in the tariff calculator**.
tariffUpdates.scope: Chapter 99 measures that reach Chapter 87 from any country: Section 232 automobiles and parts (note 33), medium- and heavy-duty vehicles, buses and parts (note 38), Section 232 metals (note 16), China Section 301 (notes 20, 31), the 2026 Section 301 actions on 60 economies and Brazil (notes 50, 52), Canada Section 338 (note 51) and the Canadian motorcycle ban, Russia's rates in lieu of column 2 (note 30), the scheduled Nicaragua duty (note 29), and the ended IEEPA and Section 122 duties. The optional certified-parts headings (9903.94.07, 9903.74.09 and the country versions) are explained but not priced. For the rate each supplier pays, see Rates by country.

inEffect.country: All countries (Japan, EU, Korea and UK at deal rates; USMCA on non-U.S. content)
inEffect.measure: Section 232 passenger vehicles and light trucks
inEffect.exemption: Covers 74 lines: cars, SUVs, crossovers, minivans and cargo vans of 8703.22–8703.90 and light trucks of 8704.21, 8704.31, 8704.41, 8704.51 and 8704.60 (note 33(b)), new or used. Collected also when an FTA rate is claimed. Products of Japan (9903.94.41), the EU (9903.94.51) and Korea (9903.94.61) pay 15% in total instead, or nothing extra when the base rate is already 15% or more (light trucks). UK cars pay 7.5% on top of 2.5% within a 100,000-vehicle annual quota (9903.94.31). USMCA-qualifying vehicles pay 25% only on the non-U.S. content Commerce has approved (9903.94.03), the U.S. content entering at 0% (9903.94.02). Vehicles at least 25 years old (9903.94.04) and articles of these lines that are not cars or light trucks (9903.94.02) pay no Section 232 duty. Section 232 vehicles do not pay the metals duties or the 2026 Section 301 duty (note 52(f)(2)).
inEffect.whatItMeans: A $40,000 car pays $11,000 from Taiwan or India, $6,000 from Japan, Germany or Korea, $4,000 from the UK within the quota.

inEffect.country: All countries (Japan, EU, Korea, Taiwan 15%; UK 10%; USMCA parts exempt)
inEffect.exemption: Covers 119 Chapter 87 lines on the note 33(g) list: chassis (8706), bodies (8707), most parts of 8708 (bumpers, body parts, brakes, gearboxes, axles, wheels, suspension, radiators, steering, airbags) and some trailer parts (8716). Charged when the article is a part of a passenger vehicle or light truck. Japan (9903.94.43), the EU (9903.94.53), Korea (9903.94.63) and Taiwan (9903.94.67, from May 1, 2026) pay 15% in total; UK parts of note 33(j) pay 10% (9903.94.32). USMCA-qualifying parts of Canada and Mexico pay nothing (9903.94.06) until Commerce sets up a non-U.S.-content process. Auto parts do not also pay the metals duties or the 2026 Section 301 duty (note 52(f)(3)). An optional heading (9903.94.07, and 9903.94.33–.69 for the deal partners) lets importers certify other parts for U.S. vehicle production or repair at the same rates instead of the metals duties.
inEffect.whatItMeans: $100,000 of brake parts pays $27,500 from India, $15,000 from Japan or Germany, nothing from Mexico with USMCA, $52,500 from China.

inEffect.country: All countries (USMCA trucks on non-U.S. content)
inEffect.measure: Section 232 medium- and heavy-duty vehicles and buses
inEffect.exemption: Covers 58 lines of note 38(b) (road tractors 8701.21–8701.29, trucks over 5 t G.V.W., dumpers and electric trucks of 8704, some special-purpose vehicles of 8705, truck chassis of 8706 and works trucks of 8709) at 25%, and the 10 bus lines of 8702 at 10%, from November 1, 2025. No country deal rates. USMCA-qualifying trucks pay 25% on the non-U.S. content Commerce approved (9903.74.03); buses have no such option and pay 10% even with USMCA. Vehicles at least 25 years old (9903.74.07) and articles that are not medium- or heavy-duty vehicles (9903.74.05) are exempt. No metals duty and no 2026 Section 301 duty (note 52(f)(5)).
inEffect.whatItMeans: A $150,000 heavy truck from Germany pays 25% + 25% = $75,000; a $400,000 coach from Canada pays $40,000.

inEffect.measure: Section 232 medium- and heavy-duty vehicle parts
inEffect.exemption: Covers the 103 Chapter 87 lines of note 38(i) (mostly 8708, plus chassis, cabs and works-truck parts) when the article is a part of a medium- or heavy-duty truck or bus. No country deal rates. USMCA-qualifying parts pay nothing (9903.74.10). Not also charged the metals duties or the 2026 Section 301 duty (note 52(f)(6)). An optional heading (9903.74.09) covers certified truck parts outside the list.
inEffect.whatItMeans: $100,000 of axles for heavy trucks from Germany pays 2.5% + 25% = $27,500; from Mexico with USMCA, nothing.

inEffect.country: All countries (deal partners 15% on mobile equipment)
inEffect.measure: Section 232 metals: trailers, farm and mobile equipment, some parts
inEffect.now: +25%, or 15% in total for farm and fixed equipment
inEffect.exemption: 88 lines are on the note 16(c) metals lists. Trailers and trailer parts (8716), some 8708 parts, snow vehicles and golf carts pay 25% (lists (vi)–(vii), 9903.82.09). Farm tractors (8701.30.10, 8701.91.10–8701.95.10), ATVs (8703.21.01) and farm-tractor chassis pay 15% in total (list (x), 9903.82.10). Crawler and other tractors, mobile cranes and drilling derricks (list (xi)) pay 25% through 2027, 15% in total for Japan, the EU, Korea, Taiwan, the UK, Switzerland and other deal partners (9903.82.22), and 25% on the non-U.S. content for USMCA goods (9903.82.20). At least 85% U.S.-melted metal: 10% (9903.82.06, .07). Goods that pay the vehicle or parts duties do not also pay these.
inEffect.whatItMeans: A $50,000 semi-trailer from Mexico pays $12,500; a $100,000 farm tractor from Japan or India pays $15,000.

inEffect.measure: Section 301: Lists 1–4A, note 31 (electric vehicles 100%) and the 2026 action
inEffect.now: +25% or +7.5% on top of Section 232; +100% on electric vehicles; +12.5% on lines outside Section 232
inEffect.exemption: List 1 (9903.88.01) covers most cars, trucks, buses and tractors (107 lines), List 2 (9903.88.02) 43 lines, List 3 (9903.88.03) parts, trailers and bicycles (195 lines), List 4A (9903.88.15, 7.5%) 22 lines. Note 31 (9903.91.03) charges 100% on electric and plug-in hybrid cars and buses since September 27, 2024. These stack with Section 232. The 12.5% 2026 duty (9903.05.31) applies only to the lines outside Section 232 (motorcycles, bicycles, wheelchairs, strollers, cycle parts). Intermodal chassis will pay 100% from November 10, 2026 (9903.91.12). USTR confirmed on October 7, 2026 that the 2018 actions continue.
inEffect.whatItMeans: A Chinese EV pays 127.5%, a Chinese gasoline car 52.5%, Chinese car parts 52.5%, a Chinese bicycle 43%.

inEffect.country: 60 Section 301 economies (Japan, EU, Korea, Taiwan, Vietnam, India, Thailand, UK, Canada, Mexico and others)
inEffect.now: +10% or +12.5% (EU, Japan, Korea, Taiwan: 10% or 12.5% in place of the base rate) on goods outside Section 232
inEffect.exemption: Does not apply to Section 232 vehicles, parts or metals goods (note 52(f), 9903.05.90), so in Chapter 87 it reaches motorcycles and e-bikes (8711), bicycles (8712), wheelchairs (8713), cycle parts (8714), strollers (8715), tanks (8710), and the parts and vehicles of other lines that are not used as listed. USMCA-qualifying goods of Canada and Mexico are exempt (9903.05.93, 9903.05.94).
inEffect.whatItMeans: A $10,000 motorcycle from Thailand or Vietnam pays $1,250; from India $1,000.

inEffect.exemption: Does not apply to Section 232 vehicles, parts or metals goods (note 50(a)(vi)), which pay only Section 232. Other Chapter 87 lines from Brazil pay 25% (9903.05.01) and 12.5% (9903.05.27).
inEffect.whatItMeans: A Brazilian car pays 27.5%; a Brazilian motorcycle 37.5% plus its base rate.

inEffect.measure: Section 338 (Canada), list 51(b)(3), and the motorcycle import ban
inEffect.now: +50% on golf carts, snow and off-road vehicles; motorcycles over 800 cc banned
inEffect.exemption: Charged even when USMCA is claimed and, since September 15, 2026, in addition to Section 232: golf carts and other snow or off-road vehicles of 8703.10.50 pay 25% + 50% = 75%, ATVs and side-by-sides of 8703.21.01 15% + 50% = 65%. Motorcycles over 800 cc (8711.50) were on the list from August 22, 2026 and are excluded from importation since September 29, 2026 (Proclamation 11063). Canadian cars, trucks and parts are not on the list.
inEffect.whatItMeans: A $15,000 Canadian side-by-side pays $9,750; Canadian motorcycles over 800 cc cannot be entered.

inEffect.measure: Russia: 35% in lieu of column 2, plus Section 232
inEffect.before: 35% in place of column 2 on 93 lines
inEffect.now: Column 2 rate, or 35% in its place, plus the Section 232 duties
inEffect.exemption: Russia pays column 2 rates, or 35% in their place on the note 30(b) lines (93 Chapter 87 lines, Proclamation 10420 of 2022), plus Section 232 and, outside Section 232, 12.5% under Section 301 (9903.05.66). Aluminum derivatives of Russia pay 200% (9903.85.68). U.S. imports of Chapter 87 goods from Russia are negligible.
inEffect.whatItMeans: A Russian car of a note 30(b) line pays 35% plus the 25% Section 232 duty.

changes.title: No Chapter 87 base-rate changes
changes.detail: 396 of 402 Chapter 87 lines carry the same General, Special and Column 2 rates in the 2026 Revision 21 as in the 2025 Basic Edition. Six statistical lines were added by splitting existing ones at unchanged rates.

changes.title: China: 100% on intermodal chassis from November 10, 2026
changes.detail: Under USTR's Section 301 action on China's maritime, logistics and shipbuilding sectors, intermodal chassis and their subassemblies and parts of 8716.39.00.90, 8716.90.30 and 8716.90.50 will pay +100% (9903.91.12) from November 10, 2026, on top of List 3 (25%). The start was suspended until then.

changes.title: Section 301 tariff on Nicaragua phases in from 2027
changes.detail: Products of Nicaragua that are not CAFTA-DR originating goods will pay +10% from January 1, 2027 and +15% from January 1, 2028 (9903.89.01, U.S. note 29). The rate is 0% in 2026.

changes.title: Metals equipment rates rise on January 1, 2028
changes.detail: Under Proclamations 11021 and 11032, the 15% total rate for farm and fixed equipment (farm tractors, ATVs) and the 15% deal rate for mobile equipment (crawler tractors, cranes) end on December 31, 2027; from January 1, 2028 these lines pay the 25% derivative rate (UK 15%, U.S.-melted 10%).

changes.title: Canadian motorcycles over 800 cc banned from import
changes.detail: Proclamation 11063 excludes motorcycles over 800 cc (8711.50) that are products of Canada from importation into the United States from September 29, 2026, in response to Canada's treatment of U.S. motor vehicles. They had paid the 50% Section 338 duty from August 22, 2026.

changes.title: Brake drums: compacted graphite iron drums circumvent the China orders (preliminary)
changes.detail: Commerce preliminarily found that compacted graphite iron brake drums from China are later-developed merchandise circumventing the 2025 antidumping and countervailing duty orders on brake drums (8708.30) from China.

changes.title: Section 338 duty on Canadian golf carts and off-road vehicles
changes.detail: Proclamation 11065 added golf carts and other snow or off-road vehicles (8703.10.50) and small off-road vehicles of 8703.21.01 (ATVs, side-by-sides) to the note 51(b)(3) list at +50% (9903.03.14), and from September 15, 2026 the duty applies in addition to Section 232. It is charged even on USMCA goods.

changes.title: Van-type trailers: final findings on China, preliminary on Canada and Mexico
changes.detail: Commerce made final affirmative dumping and subsidy determinations on van-type trailers and subassemblies (8716.39) from China (August 31, 2026), and preliminary dumping findings on Canada and Mexico (August 4, 2026), with cash deposits on the preliminary findings. Orders depend on the ITC's final votes.

changes.title: Section 338 duty on Canadian motorcycles
changes.detail: Proclamation 11048 put +50% (9903.03.14) on products of Canada on the note 51(b)(3) list, including motorcycles over 800 cc (8711.50); the start moved from August 19 to August 22, 2026 (Proclamation 11056). The motorcycles were banned from September 29, 2026.

changes.title: Chassis orders on China: sunset findings
changes.detail: Commerce found that revoking the 2021 antidumping and countervailing duty orders on chassis and subassemblies (8716.39, 8716.90) from China would likely lead to continued dumping and subsidies; the orders remain in place.

changes.title: 2026 Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies: Section 232 vehicles and parts exempt
changes.detail: The 10% or 12.5% duties on goods of 60 economies (9903.05.20–9903.05.84) took effect. They do not apply to Section 232 vehicles, parts or metals goods (note 52(f)), so in Chapter 87 they reach motorcycles, bicycles, wheelchairs, cycle parts, strollers and tanks. USMCA goods are exempt.

changes.title: Section 122 surcharge expired
changes.detail: The 10% surcharge on products of all countries (9903.03.01) expired at the close of July 23, 2026. It did not apply in addition to Section 232 duties (Proclamation 11012); in Chapter 87 it reached motorcycles, bicycles and other lines outside Section 232, and not USMCA goods.

changes.title: Section 301 tariff on Brazil: Section 232 goods exempt
changes.detail: The 25% duty on goods of Brazil (9903.05.01) took effect. Section 232 vehicles, parts and metals goods are excluded (note 50(a)(vi)).

changes.title: New AD/CVD orders on chassis from Mexico, Thailand and Vietnam
changes.detail: Commerce issued antidumping duty orders on chassis and subassemblies (8716.39, 8716.90) from Mexico, Thailand and Vietnam, and countervailing duty orders on Mexico and Thailand.

changes.title: Proclamation 11032: farm and mobile equipment rates
changes.detail: From June 8, 2026, mobile industrial equipment (crawler and other tractors of 8701.30.50 and 8701.91.50–8701.95.50, mobile cranes, drilling derricks) pays 25% through 2027, 15% in total for Japan, the EU, Korea, Taiwan, the UK, Switzerland and other deal partners (9903.82.22), and 25% on the non-U.S. content for USMCA goods (9903.82.20). Farm tractors stay at 15% in total. U.S.-melted content counts from 85%.

changes.title: Taiwan: 15% auto parts rate
changes.detail: Under the U.S.–Taiwan trade and security agreement, passenger-vehicle parts of Taiwan pay 15% in total (9903.94.67) instead of +25%. Taiwanese cars still pay 27.5%.

changes.title: Section 232 metals rebuilt: trailers 25%, farm equipment 15% total
changes.detail: Proclamation 11021 charged the metals duties on the full customs value and set new rates: 25% for derivative articles of lists (vi)–(viii) such as trailers and some vehicle parts (9903.82.09), and 15% in total for agricultural and fixed industrial equipment of lists (ix)–(x) such as farm tractors (9903.82.10) through 2027. Goods that pay the vehicle or parts duties do not also pay the metals duties.

changes.title: Steel wheels: circumvention inquiries
changes.detail: Commerce opened circumvention inquiries on whether steel wheels completed in Thailand and elsewhere circumvent the antidumping and countervailing duty orders on steel wheels (8708.70, 8716.90) from China, continued in November 2024 (22.5–24.5 inch) and March 2025 (12–16.5 inch trailer wheels).

changes.title: All IEEPA tariffs end
changes.detail: After the Supreme Court held on February 20, 2026 (Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump) that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs, Executive Order 14389 ended the Canada, Mexico, China and reciprocal duties from February 24, 2026. Section 232 vehicle and parts duties were not affected. Section 232 vehicles and parts had not paid the Canada and Mexico IEEPA duties (note 33(a)) or the reciprocal tariff.

changes.title: South Korea: 15% on cars and parts
changes.detail: Under the U.S.–Korea agreement, Korean cars, light trucks (9903.94.61) and auto parts (9903.94.63) pay 15% in total in place of the base rate and the 25%, retroactive to November 1, 2025. Light trucks, whose base rate is 25%, pay nothing extra.

changes.title: Section 232 on heavy trucks (25%), buses (10%) and truck parts (25%)
changes.detail: Proclamation 10984 put +25% on medium- and heavy-duty trucks and road tractors (9903.74.01) and their parts (9903.74.08), and +10% on buses (9903.74.02), from November 1, 2025. USMCA trucks pay on non-U.S. content (9903.74.03); USMCA parts are exempt (9903.74.10); buses get no USMCA relief. It also created an import adjustment offset for U.S. truck production.

changes.title: Japan: 15% on cars and parts
changes.detail: Under the U.S.–Japan agreement, Japanese cars and light trucks (9903.94.41) and auto parts (9903.94.43) pay 15% in total in place of the base rate and the 25% from September 16, 2025.

changes.title: AD/CVD orders on golf carts and other low-speed vehicles from China
changes.detail: Commerce issued antidumping and countervailing duty orders on certain low-speed personal transportation vehicles (golf carts and similar) from China.

changes.title: AD/CVD orders on brake drums from China and Türkiye
changes.detail: Commerce issued antidumping and countervailing duty orders on certain brake drums (8708.30) from China and Türkiye.

changes.title: European Union: 15% on cars and parts
changes.detail: Under the U.S.–EU framework, EU cars and light trucks (9903.94.51) and auto parts (9903.94.53) pay 15% in total in place of the base rate and the 25%, retroactive to August 1, 2025 (notice published September 25, 2025).

changes.title: United Kingdom: 10% on cars within a quota and on parts
changes.detail: Under the U.S.–UK Economic Prosperity Deal, UK passenger cars pay +7.5% (10% with the 2.5% base rate) within an annual quota (9903.94.31), 100,000 vehicles from 2026, and listed UK parts pay 10% in total (9903.94.32). UK light trucks and cars over the quota pay 25%.

changes.title: Section 232 on auto parts: 25%
changes.detail: Proclamation 10908 put +25% (9903.94.05) on the listed auto parts from May 3, 2025, collected also when an FTA rate is claimed. USMCA-qualifying parts stay duty-free (9903.94.06) until Commerce sets a process for their non-U.S. content.

changes.title: Non-stacking order and import adjustment offset
changes.detail: Executive Order 14289 said vehicles and parts subject to the Section 232 auto duties do not also pay the metals duties or the Canada and Mexico IEEPA duties. Proclamation 10925 created an import adjustment offset that lets U.S. vehicle assemblers offset part of the auto parts duty.

changes.title: Section 232 on cars and light trucks: 25%
changes.detail: Proclamation 10908 put +25% (9903.94.01) on imported passenger vehicles and light trucks from April 3, 2025, new or used, collected also when an FTA rate is claimed. USMCA-qualifying vehicles pay it only on their non-U.S. content once Commerce approves the U.S.-content value (9903.94.03; CBP guidance July 2025).

changes.title: Reciprocal tariff excludes Section 232 vehicles and parts
changes.detail: Executive Order 14257 set the reciprocal tariffs from April 5, 2025 but excluded goods subject to Section 232, including vehicles and auto parts. It reached motorcycles, bicycles and other Chapter 87 lines outside Section 232. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: IEEPA duties on Canada and Mexico
changes.detail: +25% on goods of Canada and Mexico from March 4, 2025; USMCA goods were exempted from March 7, 2025, and vehicles and parts under Section 232 did not pay them. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: China Section 301: 100% on electric vehicles
changes.detail: After its four-year review, USTR raised the Section 301 duty on Chinese electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles (note 31(d), 9903.91.03) from 25% to 100% from September 27, 2024.

changes.title: China Section 301 List 1: 25% on most vehicles
changes.detail: USTR's first Section 301 action put 25% on Chinese cars, trucks, buses, tractors and many other vehicles from July 6, 2018 (List 1, 9903.88.01); later lists added parts, trailers and bicycles (2018–2019).

understandIndustry.why:
U.S. imports of Chapter 87 vehicles and parts were **$337.95B in 2025**, -13.7% from $391.46B in 2024, the record year. The five largest suppliers were Mexico ($124.20B), Japan ($46.22B), Canada ($45.82B), South Korea ($38.30B) and Germany ($27.82B). Cars and SUVs (8703) were $183.83B, parts (8708) $84.68B and trucks (8704) $41.68B; together 92% of the chapter.

2025 was the first year of the Section 232 auto tariffs: 25% on cars from April 3 and on parts from May 3, cut to 15% for the EU, Japan and Korea later in the year. Car imports fell 16.3% and parts 5.8%. Imports from Germany fell 20.2%, from the UK 29.4%, from China 26.5% and from Korea 15.6%; Mexico, mostly USMCA-qualifying, fell 9.5%.

2025 is the latest full year of U.S. trade data. Duty-collected figures aren't available from an official source yet.

industryAreas.intro:
Each cell is the base rate for that product group plus the extra duties for that country, minus any preference, from the current tariff schedule. Cars and SUVs pay **27.5%** (2.5% + 25%) from most countries, **15%** from Japan, the EU and Korea, **10%** from the UK within its quota, **25%** on the non-U.S. content of USMCA cars, and **52.5%** (EVs **127.5%**) from China. Trucks of 8704 start from a 25% base rate, so they pay **50%** from most countries.

Parts depend on what they are used in: cells show **auto-part** (parts of cars and light trucks), **truck-part** (medium- and heavy-duty trucks and buses), **vehicle-part** (both at the same rate) and **other-use** (anything else, e.g. parts for farm tractors). USMCA parts are Free as auto or truck parts. Motorcycles, bicycles and other lines outside Section 232 pay the 2026 Section 301 duties (10% or 12.5%). The table does **not** include antidumping or countervailing duties (see Tariff updates).

rule.label: USMCA cars and trucks pay 25% on the non-U.S. content Commerce approved (9903.94.03, 9903.74.03; 25% of the full value without an approval, shown); USMCA auto and truck parts pay nothing (9903.94.06, 9903.74.10); buses 10% either way. Without USMCA: cars 27.5%, trucks 50%, parts 27.5%. Trailers and other metals goods pay 25% with or without USMCA. Lines outside Section 232 pay 10% (9903.05.55) unless USMCA is claimed. Mexican chassis and van trailers face AD/CVD, not shown.

Ranges like "Free · 11.8%" mean the group has lines with different base rates; select a cell to see which lines carry which rate.
Preferences: USMCA (S) is applied for Canada and Mexico on the "USMCA-qualifying" side; KR for South Korea. GSP (A, A+) has lapsed and is not applied. Other preferences are not applied.
Any other country shows the range across every country not listed (column 2 countries — Cuba, North Korea, Russia, Belarus — aside), without preferences.

Parts show one total per use when the duty depends on it: auto-part (parts of passenger vehicles and light trucks, Section 232 auto parts duty), truck-part (parts of medium- and heavy-duty trucks and buses), vehicle-part (both at the same rate), other-use (neither, e.g. parts for farm tractors or other vehicles); combined labels name the uses that share a rate. Each was checked line by line against the calculator engine.
USMCA cars and trucks are shown at 25% of the full value: the duty falls to 25% of the non-U.S. content only after Commerce approves the U.S.-content value (9903.94.02/.03, 9903.74.03/.06).

Conditional relief is not applied (it needs the importer's confirmation): vehicles at least 25 years old (9903.94.04, 9903.74.07), articles of the listed lines that are not passenger vehicles or not medium- or heavy-duty vehicles (9903.94.02, 9903.74.05), the UK quota running out, U.S.- or UK-melted metal, and the China Section 301 product exclusions.

The optional certified-parts headings (9903.94.07, 9903.74.09 and the country versions 9903.94.33, .45, .55, .65, .69) are not priced: they let importers certify parts outside the auto and truck parts lists for U.S. vehicle production or repair, paying the auto parts rates instead of the metals duties.
The IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the Section 122 surcharge (9903.03.01) expired July 23, 2026; neither is applied.

Antidumping and countervailing duties are not included: golf carts and other low-speed vehicles (China), chassis (China, Mexico, Thailand, Vietnam), brake drums (China, Türkiye), steel wheels (China), and the van-type trailer investigations (China, Canada, Mexico).

tariffEngineering.h1: HTS Chapter 87: Vehicles Other Than Railway or Tramway Rolling Stock, and Parts — Import Documents & Ways to Lower Duty

seo.title: Importing Cars, Trucks & Auto Parts: Section 232 Entry, USMCA Content, Deal Rates & Ways to Lower Duty (HTS Ch. 87) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: The rules for each HTS Chapter 87 line: Section 232 auto, truck and parts headings, USMCA U.S.-content approvals, the 15% deal rates, UK quota, EPA and DOT entry forms, 25-year-old vehicles, marking, AD/CVD scope, plus the legal ways to pay less.

tariffEngineering.intro:
For Chapter 87 the Section 232 heading decides most of the duty. Cars and light trucks enter with **9903.94.01** (or the Japan, EU, Korea, UK or USMCA heading), auto parts with **9903.94.05** (or the deal, UK or USMCA heading), heavy trucks with **9903.74.01**, buses **9903.74.02**, truck parts **9903.74.08**, all reported next to the Chapter 87 number. Vehicles also need **EPA and DOT entry declarations** (forms 3520-1 and HS-7).

The legal ways to pay less: **USMCA** (parts Free, vehicles on non-U.S. content after Commerce approves it), **origin in a deal country** (15% in total; UK 10%), the **25-year rule** for classic vehicles, **correct classification and end use** (a part used in farm equipment is not an auto part), the **certified-parts** election, and checking **AD/CVD scope**. Each rule and lever links to its regulation or proclamation.

levers.title: Qualify for USMCA
levers.saves: The whole auto or truck parts duty on parts; the duty on the U.S. content of cars and trucks; the 2.5% (cars) or 25% (trucks) base rate; the 2026 Section 301 duty on other lines
levers.appliesTo: Vehicles, parts and other goods of Canada or Mexico that meet the USMCA rules of origin (including the automotive regional value content rules)
levers.document: A USMCA certification of origin; for vehicles, a Commerce-approved U.S.-content value (entered on a separate 9903.94.02 / 9903.74.06 line, CSMS 65649652 and 68559236).
levers.caveat: Buses pay 10% even with USMCA. Golf carts, off-road vehicles and big motorcycles of Canada pay or are banned under Section 338 regardless. Metals goods (trailers) pay 25% with or without USMCA.

levers.title: Buy from a deal partner
levers.saves: Cars, light trucks and parts pay 15% in total from Japan, the EU or Korea (parts also Taiwan) instead of 27.5%; UK cars 10% within the quota, listed UK parts 10%
levers.appliesTo: 8703, light trucks of 8704, and the auto parts lines (8706–8708, some 8716)
levers.document: Proof of origin (the good must be a product of the partner under the normal non-preferential origin rules) and entry under the country heading.
levers.caveat: No deal rate for heavy trucks, buses or truck parts. Light trucks with a 25% base rate get no reduction. UK quota is 100,000 cars a year; over it, 25%.

levers.title: Classify by real use: auto, truck or other
levers.saves: The 25% auto or truck parts duty when the part is for other vehicles (other-use), or the difference between vehicle and metals rates
levers.appliesTo: Parts of 8706–8708 and 8716 on the note 33(g) and 38(i) lists
levers.document: Customer contracts, drawings and end-use records showing the vehicle the part is for; a CBP binding ruling when unsure.
levers.caveat: The duty follows the article's use: CBP can ask for proof. Misstating end use is a penalty case.

levers.title: Certify other parts for U.S. vehicle production or repair
levers.saves: Parts outside the auto and truck parts lists pay the auto parts rate (25%, or 15% for deal partners, 10% UK) instead of the metals duties
levers.appliesTo: Parts outside note 33(g) and 38(i) used to make or repair vehicles in the United States (not chapters 72, 73 or 76)
levers.document: Importer's certification that the parts will be used for U.S. automobile or truck production or repair, entered under 9903.94.07 (or 9903.94.33–.69) or 9903.74.09.
levers.caveat: Opt-in; worth it only when the metals duty would be higher. The certification must be supportable.

levers.caveat: The 2026 Section 301 duty still applies to these entries (they are not listed in note 52(f)).

seo.title: Car & Auto Parts Tariffs FAQ: Are They Still in Effect? Japan, Mexico, Canada, Germany, China, UK, HS Codes (HTS Ch. 87) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: Answers to what people search about U.S. car, truck and auto parts tariffs: whether the 25% auto tariff is still in effect, rates for Japan, Mexico, Canada, Germany, Korea, the UK and China, USMCA, Chinese EVs, heavy trucks, motorcycles, golf carts, and HS codes.
keywords: is the 25 auto tariff still in effect

finalConclusion.intro: Straight answers to the most-searched questions about U.S. tariffs on cars, trucks, auto parts and other vehicles, by country and by HS code. Each answer links to the page with the detail and the official sources.
keyTakeaways: Cars, SUVs and light trucks pay +25% under Section 232 since April 3, 2025, auto parts +25% since May 3, 2025. Japan, the EU and Korea pay 15% in total (Taiwan for parts); the UK 10% on 100,000 cars a year; USMCA parts are Free and USMCA vehicles pay on non-U.S. content.
Heavy trucks, road tractors and truck parts pay +25% and buses +10% since November 1, 2025, with no deal rates. Trucks of 8704 also carry a 25% base rate, so most pay 50%.

China pays Section 301 on top: 127.5% on electric cars, 52.5% on gasoline cars and parts. Motorcycles, bicycles and other lines outside Section 232 pay the 2026 Section 301 duties (10%–12.5%). Canadian golf carts and ATVs pay +50% and Canadian motorcycles over 800 cc are banned.
In 2025 the U.S. imported $337.95B of Chapter 87 goods, Mexico ($124.20B) and Japan ($46.22B) first.

faqs.question: Is the 25% auto tariff still in effect?
searchedAs: is the 25 auto tariff still in effect
are car tariffs still in effect
are auto tariffs still in effect
are auto tariffs in effect now
faqs.answer: Yes. The Section 232 duty of 25% on cars and light trucks (from April 3, 2025) and on auto parts (from May 3, 2025) is in the current tariff schedule (2026 Revision 21), with 15% total rates for Japan, the EU and Korea and 10% for UK cars in quota. The Supreme Court's February 20, 2026 ruling ended only the IEEPA tariffs; the auto tariffs rest on Section 232 and were not affected.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on cars from Japan?
searchedAs: tariff on used cars from japan
are there tariffs on japanese cars
faqs.answer: 15% in total for Japanese cars, SUVs and auto parts (9903.94.41, 9903.94.43) since September 16, 2025, instead of 2.5% + 25%. Japanese light trucks, with a 25% base rate, pay 25% and nothing more. Heavy trucks and truck parts get no deal rate (25% plus base). Used cars pay the same unless at least 25 years old. Japan shipped $46.22B in 2025.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on cars from Mexico?
searchedAs: us tariffs on cars from mexico
tariff on cars made in mexico
tariffs on auto parts from mexico
faqs.answer: USMCA-qualifying Mexican cars pay 25% on their non-U.S. content once Commerce approves the U.S.-content value (25% of the full value until then), with no base rate. Non-qualifying cars pay 27.5%. USMCA-qualifying auto and truck parts pay nothing. Heavy trucks: 25% on non-U.S. content with USMCA, 50% without. Mexico shipped $124.20B in 2025, over a third of the chapter.

faqs.question: What are the auto tariffs on Canada?
searchedAs: tariff on cars from canada to us
tariffs on car parts from canada to us
faqs.answer: Same USMCA rules as Mexico: qualifying cars and trucks pay 25% on non-U.S. content, qualifying parts nothing, buses 10%. Canada also pays Section 338: 50% more on golf carts and snow vehicles (75% in total) and ATVs and side-by-sides (65%), and its motorcycles over 800 cc are banned from September 29, 2026. Canada shipped $45.82B in 2025.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on cars from Germany and the EU?
searchedAs: are there tariffs on german cars
tariff on car parts from germany
faqs.answer: 15% in total for EU cars, SUVs, light trucks and auto parts (9903.94.51, 9903.94.53), retroactive to August 1, 2025. EU heavy trucks pay 25% plus the 25% base rate (50%); road tractors 29%. Germany shipped $27.82B in 2025.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on cars from South Korea?
searchedAs: tariffs on cars from south korea
faqs.answer: 15% in total for Korean cars, SUVs and auto parts (9903.94.61, 9903.94.63), retroactive to November 1, 2025. Korean light trucks pay their 25% base rate only. Korea shipped $38.30B in 2025.

faqs.question: What is the U.S. tariff on cars from the UK?
faqs.answer: 10% in total (2.5% + 7.5%, heading 9903.94.31) on UK passenger cars within an annual quota of 100,000 vehicles from 2026; above it, 27.5%. Listed UK auto parts pay 10% (9903.94.32). UK light trucks pay 50%.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on Chinese cars and electric vehicles?
faqs.answer: 127.5% on Chinese electric and plug-in hybrid cars: 2.5% base + 100% Section 301 (note 31, since September 27, 2024) + 25% Section 232. Chinese gasoline cars pay 52.5% (2.5% + 25% List 1 + 25%), trucks 75%, auto parts 52.5%. China shipped $13.23B of Chapter 87 goods in 2025, mostly parts.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on auto parts?
faqs.answer: Listed auto parts (U.S. note 33(g): engines, transmissions, axles, brakes, body parts, bumpers, wheels, seats and many more) pay 2.5% + 25% = 27.5% from most countries; 15% in total from Japan, the EU, Korea and Taiwan; 10% for listed UK parts; nothing for USMCA-qualifying parts; 52.5% from China. Parts of heavy trucks pay 25% plus base with no deal rates. Parts not on the lists pay the metals or other duties.

faqs.question: What are the tariffs on trucks and the chicken tax?
faqs.answer: Trucks of 8704 carry a 25% base rate (the "chicken tax"). Section 232 adds 25%: light trucks via the auto duty (from April 3, 2025), medium- and heavy-duty trucks and road tractors via 9903.74.01 (from November 1, 2025), so most pay 50%. Japanese, EU and Korean light trucks pay 25% in total. USMCA trucks pay 25% on non-U.S. content and no base rate. Buses pay +10%.

faqs.question: Does USMCA exempt cars and auto parts from the tariff?
faqs.answer: Partly. USMCA-qualifying parts of cars and trucks pay no Section 232 duty (9903.94.06, 9903.74.10). USMCA-qualifying cars and trucks pay 25% on the value of their non-U.S. content, after Commerce approves the U.S.-content figure; until then, 25% of the full value. Buses and metals goods such as trailers get no USMCA relief.

faqs.question: Is there a tariff on motorcycles?
faqs.answer: Motorcycles (8711) are outside Section 232. They pay their base rate (Free or 2.4%) plus the 2026 Section 301 duty: 12.5% for Japan (in place of the base rate), Thailand and Vietnam, 10% for India and the EU; Chinese motorcycles 20% to 39.9%. Canadian motorcycles over 800 cc are banned from import since September 29, 2026 (Proclamation 11063).

faqs.question: Is there a tariff on golf carts?
faqs.answer: Golf carts (8703.10.50.30) are on Section 232 metals list (vii): 2.5% + 25% = 27.5%. Chinese golf carts pay 7.5% more under Section 301 List 4A (35%), and Chinese golf carts and other low-speed personal transportation vehicles also carry the antidumping and countervailing duties ordered in August 2025. Canadian golf carts pay 50% more under Section 338: 75%.

faqs.question: Is there a tariff on bicycles?
faqs.answer: Bicycles (8712) pay 3.7% to 11% and are outside Section 232. The 2026 Section 301 duty applies: 10% in place of the base rate for Taiwan, 12.5% on top for Vietnam. Chinese bicycles pay the base rate + 25% (List 3) + 12.5%: up to 48.5%.

faqs.question: What are the HS codes for cars and auto parts?
faqs.answer: Cars and SUVs are in 8703 (by engine: 8703.21–8703.24 gasoline, 8703.31–8703.33 diesel, 8703.40–8703.70 hybrids, 8703.80 electric); trucks in 8704; buses 8702; tractors 8701. Auto parts are mostly 8708: bumpers 8708.10, body parts 8708.29, brakes 8708.30, gearboxes 8708.40, axles 8708.50, wheels 8708.70, suspension 8708.80, other parts 8708.99. Engines (8407, 8408), tires (4011) and batteries (8507) are in other chapters but are also on the auto parts list.
